extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of arithmetic/algebra (historical), and practical users such as merchants and surveyors
extracted.subtask_description: Excerpt from a historical Italian mathematics treatise covering definitions, classifications of numbers, rules and algorithms for arithmetic and algebraic operations, geometric demonstrations of algebraic facts, and practical rules for merchants (tables, measures, exchanges).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: discrete (discreta) vs continuous (continua) quantities
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguishes quantities that are discrete (numerical articles, 'articuli primi') from continuous/measurable quantities; introduces the fundamental dichotomy for arithmetic and geometry ('Divisio Discreta e continua quantitati').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that discrete quantities have indivisible units (e.g., counts of objects) while continuous quantities require geometric measure; this classification underpins later distinctions (linear, square, cubic numbers, surfaces, solids) and selection of methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of numbers: unit, prime, composite (primii, primi, composti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines prime numbers, composite numbers, units and their roles in enumeration and divisibility (discussion of 'numeri primi', 'integralmente', 'parti integrali').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives examples and consequences for divisibility and factorization; notes which numbers are measured and how primes behave with respect to parts and multiples (examples and lists of numeric examples appear throughout).

rubrics_metrics.name: Parity and divisibility rules (even/odd; division into parts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed rules about even and odd numbers, how numbers divide into parts, and how multiples relate (many paragraphs on 'pariter/impariter', numbers divisible into 2,4,8,... etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates divisibility patterns (e.g., behavior of numbers under doubling, halving, repeated doubling producing chains like 2,4,8,16...), shows how to decide whether numbers can be divided into equal integral parts, and lists many illustrative numeric patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and properties of figurate numbers (linear, square, cubic, triangular, pentagonal, circular)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines numbers by geometric form: linear (lineari), square (quadrati), cubic (cubi), triangular, pentagonal, circular, etc., and explains how multiplicative structure corresponds to geometric composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains when a number is called square (product of a number by itself), cubic (product of three equal factors), how surface/solid counts relate to sides and angles, and the proportional relations between lateral, superficial and solid numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbers of surface/superficial and solid/volumetric types and their proportions
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains distinction between surface numbers (numeri superficiali) and solid numbers (numeri solidi), how surfaces compare and how solids contain lateral and superficial counts; relationships of proportionality among them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives examples of proportional relations between surfaces and solids (e.g., how a solid relates to its faces and contained linear measures) and indicates how such numeric types are used in geometric demonstrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of square and cube roots and operations between squares and cubes
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules about taking square and cube roots, forming squares and cubes and moving between them; includes 'modo a partire da quadrati per fare cube' and vice versa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides geometric demonstrations for why squares and cubes multiply/add as they do and prescribes methods to pass from one power to another; references to tractato sections for algorithms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometric demonstration of algebraic rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Many algebraic rules (e.g., multiplication, binomial expansions, identities) are justified via geometric demonstrations ('la cagione e demoftratione geometrica').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance emphasizes using geometric constructions to prove algebraic equalities and operations; repeated cross-references to particular tractates where geometric proofs are given for algebraic operations and identities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithms for arithmetic operations by place-value (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical algorithms and rules for performing addition, subtraction, multiplication and division — including multiplication/division of multi-digit numbers and rules for 'partire, fummare e fotrare' (add and multiply).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies methods of breaking numbers into parts, using place-value techniques, and treating compounds (binomials, multinomials); references to tractato sections that give step-by-step processes and worked examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algebraic manipulation rules for binomials and multinomials
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for multiplying, dividing, summing and factoring binomials and multinomials ('binomi', 'multinomii'); includes methods for multiplying one polynomial by another and using remainders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives explicit techniques for handling binomial products, extracting residues, and applying algebraic identities; cross-references to tractato and examples showing expansions and reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation and naming of algebraic terms (description of terms and order)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanations of how to name and understand terms in algebraic expressions (e.g., first, second, third terms), and rules for ordering and cataloging terms ('descriatione del 2° termine', 'descriatione del terzo termino').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies how to interpret positions/indices in expressions, how to arrange terms in canonical order, and how to read compound expressions for computational procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables and accounting rules for merchants (taula del merito, tauola del tractato, tabelle del merito)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical mercantile rules: how to prepare accounting tables, compute 'merito' (interest/merit), manage exchanges, changes, balances and multiple payments; instructions for merchant practice and producing necessary exemplars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how merchants should construct tables, how to keep ledgers and accounts, how to compute merit/interest at term, how to handle multiple currencies and exchanges, and how to use tables for practical trading purposes (many tractate references and examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for measures, proportions, and surveying (measuring barrels, bottles, tables of measures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for measuring volumes and surfaces (e.g., 'misurare le botti', 'misurare le superfici') and creating standardized tables of measures for use in trade and geometry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives procedures to measure common containers, convert between units, and compile measurement tables; includes practical instructions for carpenters, merchants and surveyors and references tractate sections with measurement tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification and treatment of special numerical classes: perfect, abundant, deficient numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of 'numero perfetto', 'numero superabundante' (abundante) and related notions: definitions via sum of parts and their relation to the whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how to test for abundance/perfection (sum of divisors/parts compared to number), gives examples and shows consequences for number theory and classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of numeral systems and bases (binary, ternary, quaternary, etc.) and place-value formation
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of numeration systems (binary, ternary, quaternary, etc.), how numbers are formed by repeated doubling/halving and by powers of the unit base, and how different bases generate different divisibility patterns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrates how successive doubling produces sequences (2,4,8,16...), how bases define partitions into integral parts, and how to reason about divisibility and representation in various bases; provides examples of numbering chains and their arithmetic behavior.
